title: Serving runtime daily scratchpad - 2026-03-04
content:
Morning notes - triage + perf checks

Context:
- Following up on last night's kernel swap (float16-mm opt) - saw ~1.6-1.8x latency regression on long-seq (seq=2048) multi-token generation in smoke tests. Host: k8s-private-rt-03, model: rwkv-14b-quant, runtime: v2.7.1 -> v2.8.0-pr378
- Reproduced locally on dev box with same CUDA/cuDNN combos (driver: 535.54).

Immediate hypothesis:
- New GEMM kernel alignment causes more memory copies for >1024 seq paths (edge-case padding behavior).
- KV cache stride changed in the kernel shim; continuous batching interaction may be invalidating prefetch assumptions.

Repro steps (what I ran):
- ./bench/generate --model models/rwkv-14b-quant --seq 2048 --batch 1 --tokens 512 --warmup 5 --iters 20  # baseline v2.7.1: p50=110ms p95=210ms
- build/pr-378/bin/generate ...  # v2.8.0-pr378: p50=180ms p95=360ms
- perf trace: observed extra memcpy calls around step 1 and step 128 (see perf log attached to PR).

Notes from triage meeting (10:30AM):
- Sofia: confirmed regression only on long-seq and some attention variants (multi-head > 64?). Short seq (<=512) unaffected.
- Liam: kernel fallback to legacy GEMM eliminates regression but is slower on small seqs; wants targeted guard for long-seq path.
- Action: revert alignment tweak OR gate it by sequence length. Need benchmark across seq=64/256/1024/2048.

Bugs to track for today:
- SRV-1423: Latency regression after kernel changes (high). Assigned: Evan. Steps: isolate commit, add repro unit, open revert PR if needed.
- SRV-1419: KV-cache invalidation on batch merge (medium). Assigned: Sofia. Notes: observed stale keys when merging 2 continuous-batched requests with mismatched metadata headers.

Perf TODOs (priority order):
- [ ] Run full perf matrix across kernel variants (legacy, opt-align, opt-noalign) for seq = [64, 256, 1024, 2048] on g4dn and A10G. Record p50/p95 and mem usage. Estimated ~3h per node.
- [ ] Add microbenchmark around memcpy counts (instrument mm shim to count copies).
- [ ] Add unit repro test for SRV-1423 in CI (nightly slow-tests) that runs a single long-seq generation and asserts p95 < 250ms on target infra (will be flaky but useful for PR checks).
- [ ] Revisit continuous batching prefetch logic with Liam: check stride computation and alignment rounding.
- [ ] Run quantized model sanity check across kernel variants (accuracy/regression test) - 100 eval prompts sampled from regression set.

Kernel notes / things to remember:
- Alignment change was to improve vectorized loads for head_size multiple of 64. However, when seq*NKV causes unaligned tail buffer, we fall back to small-copy path. That fallback is currently executed more often due to cumulative padding behavior.
- Make guard: if seq > 1024, prefer legacy kernel or use tiled-copy strategy.
- Check nvprof traces: look for cudaMemcpyKind=DeviceToDevice that wasn't present before. D2D memcpys are expensive in our VM topology because they're not NVLINK-local on some nodes.

Quick checklist for PR flow (today):
- [ ] Create pr-379 branch: add seq-gate to kernel selector + perf flags (Evan).
- [ ] Run regression matrix on pr-379 vs pr-378 (Sofia).
- [ ] If improvement confirmed, merge and roll to canary fleet (A/B) targeting 10% of serving nodes with rollback monitor for p95 > baseline*1.2 (Liam + SRE).

Open questions:
- If we gate by seq length, is there any case where seq fluctuates mid-request (streaming)? Need to ensure streaming chunk sizes don't trigger fallback unexpectedly.
- Should the runtime expose a per-model "prefer-legacy-for-long-seq" flag in model config? Might be simplest for rollout.

Notes to self (dev commands / files):
- bench scripts: bench/long_seq.py (wraps ./generate), perf logs in /tmp/perf-2026-03-04-*.tgz
- kernel code: serving-runtime/kernels/gemm_align.cu and kernels/legacy_gemm.cu. Shim: serving-runtime/kernels/selector.cpp
- local repro command I used: 
  docker run --gpus all -v $(pwd)/models:/models --entrypoint /bin/bash pr-build -c "./bin/generate --model /models/rwkv-14b-quant --seq 2048 --tokens 512 --batch 1 --iters 20"

Quick timeline (today):
- 11:30 - finish isolation & add repro test (1.5h)
- 13:00 - run perf matrix on A10G (3h)
- 16:30 - sync w/ Liam & Sofia, decide revert vs gate (30m)
- 17:15 - open PR (if needed) and trigger canary rollout.

Other small TODOs:
- [ ] Update kernel notes doc with reproducible commands and nvprof traces (link to confluence page).
- [ ] Add a short blurb to release notes if we end up reverting: "Fixed a regression impacting long-sequence workloads introduced in v2.8.0 kernel updates."

Random thoughts / scratch lines:
- Might be worth adding a runtime-level metric for memcpy_count and memcpy_time per request (observable in Console) - high diagnostic value.
- Could also add a quick heuristic: if p95 long-seq increases > 1.3x, auto-schedule canary rollback.

End of day goal: either merged fix (seq gate) or clear revert + validated canary plan.
